about: What R8 does to each library in the release build, reviewed. R8InventoryTest fails when the release classpath or a declared dependency is missing from here, so a new library gets read before it ships. scripts/check-shrunk-build.mjs reads `expect` and checks it against the shrunk APK and R8's mapping.txt.

androidx.compose:compose-bom.why: A version table; it ships no code.

androidx.core:core-splashscreen.why: Reads theme attributes; nothing is looked up by class name.

androidx.biometric:biometric.why: Calls the framework BiometricPrompt; no field or class is read by name.

androidx.credentials:credentials.why: CredentialProviderFactory loads the Play Services provider with Class.forName; its consumer rules keep it, and expect.classes pins that.

androidx.credentials:credentials-play-se.why: The provider that Class.forName loads, plus HiddenActivity named in the manifest.

androidx.core:core-telecom.why: Binder calls into Telecom; no names are looked up.

androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-viewmodel-c.why: MainActivity's factory compares class literals; it does not look a ViewModel up by name.

androidx.lifecycle:lifecycle-process.why: Starts from an androidx.startup initializer named in the manifest; the check asserts initializers keep their names.

androidx.navigation:navigation-compose.why: The app builds no NavHost and has no type-safe routes, so no class is serialized into a route.

androidx.datastore:datastore-preferences.why: Its native shared counter calls NativeSharedCounter from JNI by name; the check reads the .so and asserts the class kept its name.

androidx.compose.ui:ui.why: Compose runtime and UI keep what their own rules name; no name lookups.

androidx.compose.material:material-icons.why: Vector data in static fields; unused icons are shrunk.

com.squareup.okhttp3:okhttp.why: Picks a TLS platform with Class.forName and starts from an androidx.startup initializer; it ships rules for both, and reads its public-suffix list from assets/ (expect.apkEntries).

org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-serializat.why: The compiler plugin writes the serializers, so field names are string constants. Companion.serializer() lookups need our rules, and expect.serializable checks each serializable class kept them.

org.jetbrains.kotlinx:kotlinx-coroutines.why: Main dispatcher and exception handler are found through ServiceLoader. R8 rewrites META-INF/services as it renames; the check confirms each provider exists.

io.coil-kt.coil3:coil-network-okhttp.why: The network fetcher registers through ServiceLoader. R8 rewrites that services file as it renames; the check confirms the provider exists.

org.osmdroid:osmdroid-android.why: Ships no rules. Only ArchiveFileFactory reflects, for offline tile archives, which this app does not open. MapView is built in code, not inflated.

com.github.team-telnyx:telnyx-webrtc-and.why: Sends its socket messages through Gson by field name, and its native library calls Java by name. Ships no rules. Renamed, calling never registers.

com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging.why: Component registrars are loaded by class name from manifest metadata; firebase-components keeps them and the check asserts it.

com.posthog:posthog-android.why: Serializes its events and remote config with Gson by field name; its consumer rules keep those classes. Reads posthog-meta.properties from assets for the mapping id the release workflow writes.

groups.androidx.appcompat: Transitive via Telnyx and Material. Views inflate by class name from XML, which aapt keeps.
groups.androidx.cardview: Transitive via Material; XML views, kept by aapt.
groups.androidx.constraintlayout: Transitive via Telnyx; XML views, kept by aapt.
groups.androidx.coordinatorlayout: Transitive via Material; XML views, kept by aapt.
groups.androidx.core: No name lookups beyond rules it ships.
groups.androidx.datastore: See direct entry; JNI checked from the .so.
groups.androidx.emoji2: Starts from an androidx.startup initializer, asserted by name.
groups.androidx.fragment: Fragments by name from XML only; none here.
groups.androidx.graphics: graphics-path calls its classes from JNI; the check reads the .so and asserts they kept their names.
groups.androidx.lifecycle: Ships rules for observers and ViewModels.
groups.androidx.profileinstaller: Starts from an androidx.startup initializer, asserted by name.
groups.androidx.recyclerview: Transitive via Material; XML views, kept by aapt.
groups.androidx.startup: Loads initializers by class name from manifest metadata; ships rules, and the check asserts every initializer kept its name.
groups.androidx.versionedparcelable: Ships rules for its Parcelable fields.
groups.androidx.window: Optional vendor classes found by name; they ship rules and fall back when absent.
groups.com.google.accompanist: Drawable painter via Telnyx; no name lookups.
groups.com.google.android.gms: Play services client stubs; ship rules.
groups.com.google.android.libraries.identity.go: Credential types for passkeys and sign-in; Parcelable and Bundle based.
groups.com.google.android.material: Transitive via Telnyx. XML views, kept by aapt; app code uses Compose Material.
groups.com.google.code.gson: Reads fields by name. This is why the Telnyx keep exists; Gson 2.12 ships rules for TypeToken and annotated fields only, so unannotated Telnyx models depend on our rule.
groups.com.google.firebase: See direct entry; registrars asserted by name.
groups.com.posthog: See direct entry; the core module ships the Gson rules for its event classes.
groups.com.squareup.curtains: Via PostHog, for session replay, which is off. Hooks window callbacks; no name lookups.
groups.com.jakewharton.timber: Via Telnyx. Tags come from caller class names, which only labels log lines.
groups.com.telnyx.webrtc.lib: Telnyx's WebRTC fork; its Java classes are called from libjingle by name. Covered by the com.telnyx.webrtc.** rule and checked from the .so.
groups.io.ktor: Via Telnyx for its HTTP calls, with a Gson serializer. Providers register through ServiceLoader, which R8 rewrites; the models it fills are Telnyx's, kept by our rule.
groups.org.jetbrains.kotlin: Stdlib only. kotlin-reflect is not on the classpath, so nothing reads Kotlin metadata at run time.
groups.org.jetbrains.kotlinx: Coroutines use ServiceLoader (checked); serialization is generated code plus our rules.
groups.org.slf4j: Via Ktor. No binder is shipped, so it logs nowhere; Ktor's rules silence the missing binder.

packages.why: Gson reads the SDK's message classes by field name and libjingle calls its Java by name. All of it keeps its name.

classes.name: androidx.credentials.playservices.CredentialProviderPlayServicesImpl
classes.why: CredentialProviderFactory loads it with Class.forName. Without it every passkey ceremony fails with no provider.

serializable.why: Each class with a generated serializer keeps its Companion field and Companion.serializer(), which kotlinx looks up by name.

enums.why: Enum.valueOf reads values(), so an enum that kept values() or valueOf() keeps them under those names.

attributes.name: Signature
attributes.why: Gson reads the generic type of the Telnyx SDK's List and Map fields from it.

attributes.name: RuntimeVisibleAnnotations
attributes.why: Gson reads @SerializedName names from it, and kotlinx.serialization reads its annotations.

apkEntries.why: OkHttp reads its public-suffix list from the APK's assets by this name.
